--- title: "Player impact from lineups" --- ::: {#takeaways .cell execution_count=1} ::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"} ## Takeaways - **Lineups rebuilt for every game since 2003-04 (NBA) and 2009 (WNBA).** In every season they account for at least 95% of points and possessions (98-100% in most). - **Player impact predicts next season better than the team's own results.** Last season's player impact, weighted by who actually plays this season, explains 54% of next-season NBA team net rating (43% WNBA), against 35% (24% WNBA) for the team's own net rating last season. - **Net rating plus our variables predicts playoff series better than net rating alone.** Adding availability-adjusted strength (this season's player impact, counting only players available for the playoffs) improves NBA series predictions (+0.012 log-likelihood per series, one-sided p = 0.07); in the WNBA the gain points the same way (p = 0.36). Details on the Championships page. - **Weighting the archetype mix by player quality did not beat quality alone.** Who is good matters more than which role they play. ::: ::: ## The model we settled on, and why | league | model | series called correctly | avg chance on eventual champion | champion in top 3 | gain over net rating (p) | |:---------|:-------------------------------------------------------------|:--------------------------|:----------------------------------|:--------------------|:---------------------------| | NBA | Net rating alone (baseline) | 70% | 15% | 54% | | | NBA | Availability-adjusted strength alone (ours) | 73% | 14% | 69% | p = 0.10 | | NBA | **Net rating + availability-adjusted strength (chosen)** | 71% | 18% | 54% | p = 0.07 | | NBA | Net + ours + star player | 71% | 18% | 62% | p = 0.02 | | NBA | Net + ours + star + archetype x quality | 70% | 18% | 69% | p = 0.36 | | NBA | Net + ours split offense/defense + archetype x quality + age | 71% | 16% | 62% | p = 0.45 | | WNBA | Net rating alone (baseline) | 71% | 30% | 80% | | | WNBA | Availability-adjusted strength alone (ours) | 72% | 27% | 80% | p = 0.26 | | WNBA | **Net rating + availability-adjusted strength (chosen)** | 72% | 35% | 80% | p = 0.36 | | WNBA | Net + ours + star player | 71% | 34% | 80% | p = 0.84 | | WNBA | Net + ours + star + archetype x quality | 65% | 36% | 80% | p = 0.75 | | WNBA | Net + ours split offense/defense + archetype x quality + age | 70% | 38% | 80% | p = 0.54 | **Why this one.** *Availability-adjusted strength* is our variable: each team rebuilt from this season's lineup-based player impact, counting only the players available for the playoffs, so a team that lost its best player late in the season is rated on the roster it will actually play with. Net rating can't see that. - **It improves on net rating at picking champions.** Average chance on the eventual champion: NBA 18% vs 15% for net rating alone; WNBA 35% vs 30%. - **Playoff series:** 71% vs 70% called correctly in the NBA. The gain over net rating alone is in the same direction but not statistically reliable on its own (one-sided p = 0.07; WNBA p = 0.36). - **Weight:** in the combined NBA model our variable holds 50% of the weight against 50% for net rating (44% vs 56% in the WNBA): the two carry about equal weight, so each adds information the other lacks. - **Why keep net rating in it.** Net rating captures things our lineup estimates miss (team scheme and coaching, and players with too few minutes to estimate well); ours captures who will actually play. Together they beat either alone. - **Star players.** Adding the best available player's impact puts the champion in the NBA top three in 62% of test seasons (vs 54% without it), so star power is used in the 2026-27 forecast (Gilgeous-Alexander, Wembanyama and Jokić drive their teams' ratings). - **Archetype x quality.** With its penalty tuned inside the season-by-season test it reaches 18% on the NBA champion and 36% in the WNBA, about the chosen model's level but not clearly above it: with 13-20 test seasons, six extra role variables add noise about as fast as signal. Who is good still explains more than which role they play. - **Honest caveat.** The player-impact version we use was chosen because it predicts unseen games best. An older version (which let last season's estimates carry over in full) gave bigger gains here, but fit unseen games worse, so we did not pick it to flatter this table. - **How it is trained.** Season by season, using only earlier seasons, with recent seasons weighted more heavily (the weighting is chosen from past seasons only). ## Other approaches we tested Everything below led to the chosen model. Roster-only versions use **last season's** player impact so that no information from the season being predicted leaks in; they show how much roster quality alone can do. ## How it is measured Every stretch of play with the same ten players on the floor (a *stint*) is one observation, **regular season only**. A ridge regression gives each player an **offense** and a **defense** effect in points per 100 possessions, holding the other nine players fixed. The ridge penalty pulls every estimate toward a **prior**: what we would expect from the player's box-score production (usage, scoring and efficiency, playmaking, rebounding, steals, blocks, turnovers), learned from other seasons. Lineup evidence moves a player away from that prior only as far as the data supports, which keeps role players who share the floor with stars from soaking up the stars' credit. **Which prior?** Four versions were tested on games the model didn't see (first half of each season fitted, second half predicted) and on predicting next season's team results. The box-score prior won both tests and is the one used everywhere. | prior | held-out fit, NBA | held-out fit, WNBA | next-season R², NBA | next-season R², WNBA | |:---------------------|--------------------:|---------------------:|----------------------:|-----------------------:| | A prev x1.0 (old) | 0.0069 | 0.0076 | 0.4978 | 0.3649 | | B prev x0.5 | 0.0067 | 0.0072 | 0.5275 | 0.3943 | | C box-score prior | 0.0082 | 0.0095 | 0.5425 | 0.4279 | | D box 0.5 + prev 0.5 | 0.0081 | 0.0091 | 0.5595 | 0.4307 | *Held-out fit* is the share of scoring variation explained in unseen stints (single stints are very noisy, so these are small numbers; what matters is the comparison). *Next-season R²* is how well last season's estimates, applied to this season's rosters, explain this season's team net rating. The old method (A) let last season's estimate carry over in full, which allowed some role players' numbers to build up year after year. **Avoiding leakage:** this season's impact, summed across a roster, rebuilds this season's net rating. So every roster-based prediction below uses **last season's** player impact applied to this season's roster. ## Top players (latest two seasons) At least 800 minutes.
